title: Knowledge, Entitlements, Milestones, Service Console, Omni-Channel, and routing
objectives: Place Knowledge articles as reusable answers, not as Case comments.
Explain Entitlements and Milestones as the SLA contract and clocks (up to 10 milestones per entitlement process).
Describe Lightning Service Console as a workspace for agents, not a routing engine.
Choose Omni-Channel routing when presence and capacity matter, versus APP-003 assignment rules alone.
diagnostic_question: Agents miss first-response clocks, cannot find approved answers, and cherry-pick easy Cases from a queue. Which of Knowledge, Entitlements, Milestones, Service Console, or Omni-Channel do you reach for first, and what would you still leave to assignment rules?
definition: After Cases exist (APP-003), this lesson is how service is delivered to standard: Knowledge is the approved article corpus; Entitlements are the customer's service contract on a Case; Milestones are required time-dependent steps on an entitlement process (first response, resolution)—up to 10 per process; Lightning Service Console is the agent workspace; Omni-Channel routes work to available agents using capacity and routing configuration. ([Milestones](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.entitlements_milestones_parent.htm); [SLA policies and milestones](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.it_srvcs_manual_sla_setup.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for whether you confuse escalation rules with milestones, queues with Omni-Channel, and Console with a routing product. Wrong SLA design creates false breaches. Knowledge that is only a shared Drive folder will not attach, version, or data-categorize like Lightning Knowledge.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hotel front desk. Knowledge is the SOP binder of approved answers. Entitlements are the guest's loyalty tier (what service they bought). Milestones are the clocks on check-in and room-ready. The Service Console is the front-desk workspace with many tabs. Omni-Channel is the dispatcher who sends the next guest to a free concierge based on who is on duty and how full their hands are—not the same as a shared waiting list from APP-003.
deeper_explanation: Milestones represent required, time-dependent steps such as first response or case resolution. They are added to entitlement processes so reps resolve support records correctly and on time. An entitlement process can have up to 10 milestones. A milestone can occur once or recur until the process exits. Review Milestone Limitations before go-live. ([Milestones](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.entitlements_milestones_parent.htm))

Milestone actions are time-dependent workflow-style actions on complete or violate. Recurrence type is chosen when you create a milestone type. Auto-applying entitlements to Cases (and similar objects) reduces manual SLA attachment. IT Services Help reuses the same SLA/milestone concepts on incidents. ([SLA policies](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.it_srvcs_manual_sla_setup.htm))

Knowledge articles are metadata-published content (draft, published, archived) distinct from Case comment data. Data categories, record types, and channels (internal, public, Experience Cloud) are configuration. Do not invent article-type limits here.

Lightning Service Console is a console app: workspace tabs, pinned lists, utilities. It does not assign Cases by itself. Omni-Channel uses presence statuses, routing configurations, and capacity so work items (Cases, chats, and others as licensed) interrupt available agents. Assignment rules (APP-003) still often land work on a queue that Omni-Channel then drains.

Routing here means Omni-Channel queue routing, skills, or Omni-Channel Flow—not Case assignment rule entries. If the org only needs a shared bay with pull, stay on queues. Mark exact Omni-Channel object lists and capacity units Needs verification per license.

mental_model.analogy: Hotel front desk: Knowledge = SOP binder, Entitlement = loyalty tier on the folio, Milestone = check-in/room-ready clocks, Service Console = the desk with many guest folios open, Omni-Channel = dispatcher assigning the next guest to a free concierge, APP-003 queue = the lobby waiting list.
useful_mapping: Knowledge article → approved SOP page agents should reuse
Entitlement → which SLA the customer purchased
Entitlement process → the clock template attached via the entitlement
Milestone → a required timed step (max 10 per process)
Milestone action → notify/update when warning, complete, or violate
Service Console → agent workspace, not a router
Case row → the guest folio (data); processes and articles → house rules (metadata)
where_it_breaks: Not every Case gets an entitlement; some orgs apply them only to premium accounts.
Omni-Channel can route objects besides Cases depending on licenses.
Knowledge publication is not the same as Files in a library (APP-006).
The analogy does not encode digital engagement, messaging, or Einstein classification.

claims.claim: Milestones are required, time-dependent steps in the support process, such as first response or case resolution, added to entitlement processes. An entitlement process can have up to 10 milestones. A milestone may occur once or recur until the process exits.

SLA policies include logic to enforce service levels. Create milestones and add them to the policy (up to 10). Milestone actions are time-dependent workflow actions on complete or violate. Recurrence type is required on milestone type. Auto-apply entitlements can attach the correct SLA to objects including Cases.
claims.validation: Configure Your Own SLA Policies and Milestones for IT Services.

claims.claim: Assignment rules still route records to a user or queue using attributes. Omni-Channel and Service Console are additional layers, not a redefinition of assignment.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Knowledge is published answers. Entitlements attach the customer's SLA. Milestones are clocks on that process—max 10. Service Console is the agent workspace. Omni-Channel dispatches by presence and capacity. Queues and assignment rules from APP-003 still feed many designs.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I separate four jobs: find an answer, honor a contract, work in a console, route to an available human. I will not call an escalation rule a milestone. I will not call the Console a router. If cherry-picking is the pain, I look at Omni-Channel. If first-response is the pain, I look at entitlement processes and milestone actions. I auto-apply entitlements when Help's feature fits so agents do not pick SLAs by memory.

terminology.plain: Approved, versioned articles agents (and sometimes customers) search instead of reinventing answers.
terminology.precise: Lightning Knowledge articles with publication states and optional data categories. Not a Case comment and not a Files library (APP-006).
terminology.example: Published article LAB_Reset_VPN attached to Case 00001012.
terminology.non_example: A long Case comment copied onto every VPN ticket.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: ContentNote / Files: document storage, not the Knowledge object model.
terminology.boundary: Article types, translation, and Experience Cloud channels: reverify Help.

terminology.plain: The service contract attached to the customer (and then the Case): what they paid for.
terminology.precise: A record that can apply an entitlement process (SLA template) to Cases or similar support objects. Can be auto-applied. Not the Case itself.
terminology.example: LAB_Gold Support entitlement on Account LAB_Northwind applied to the Case.
terminology.non_example: A Case Priority picklist value named Gold with no entitlement process.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Service Contract / Asset: often related, not synonyms.
terminology.boundary: Exact object relationships vary with Field Service vs classic support.

terminology.plain: A required timed step such as first response or resolve-by.
terminology.precise: Lives on an entitlement process. Maximum 10 per process. Once or recurring until the process exits. Actions fire on warning, completion, or violation (as configured).
terminology.example: First Response in 1 business hour on LAB_Gold process.
terminology.non_example: A Case escalation rule that emails a manager with no entitlement process.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Escalation rule (APP-003): classic Case aging without the entitlement model.
terminology.boundary: Review Milestone Limitations in Help before promising recurrence behavior.

terminology.plain: The SLA template: which milestones fire on which Cases.
terminology.precise: Metadata container for up to 10 milestones. Applied through an entitlement (often auto-applied). Distinct from a Flow interview.
terminology.example: LAB_Gold process with First Response and Resolution milestones.
terminology.non_example: A record-triggered Flow that emails if Age > 1 hour with no milestone object.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: SLA policy in IT Services simplified setup: same idea, different UI.
terminology.boundary: IT Services vs classic Entitlement Management UI differences.

terminology.plain: The Lightning console app agents use to work several records without losing context.
terminology.precise: Workspace tabs, utilities, pinned lists. Not Omni-Channel and not assignment. Requires a console app definition and navigation items.
terminology.example: Lightning Service Console with Cases, Knowledge, Omni-Channel utility.
terminology.non_example: The standard Sales Lightning app with a Cases tab.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Salesforce Classic Service Cloud Console: predecessor product.
terminology.boundary: Macros, quick text, and keyboard shortcuts are neighboring productivity features.

terminology.plain: The dispatcher that pushes or offers work to agents who are Available and have capacity.
terminology.precise: Presence statuses, routing configurations, service channels, capacity. Often drains queues that assignment rules filled. Not the Console itself.
terminology.example: Agent in Available-Cases presence receives the next LAB_Tier1 Case automatically.
terminology.non_example: A queue list view agents refresh and cherry-pick.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Assignment rule: first owner, no presence model.
terminology.boundary: Omni-Channel Flow vs standard routing: confirm which the org uses.

terminology.plain: How a work item finds an agent in Omni-Channel, beyond 'put it on a queue.'
terminology.precise: Queue-based, skills-based, or Flow-based Omni-Channel routing as licensed. Still distinct from Case assignment rule entries.
terminology.example: Skills routing: Billing skill required, capacity 2.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Email-to-Case routing address: capture, not Omni-Channel.
terminology.boundary: External routing / partner telephony: Needs verification.

terminology.plain: What Salesforce does at warning, success, or breach of a milestone.
terminology.precise: Time-dependent workflow actions on the SLA/milestone, such as notify or field update when a milestone is completed or violated.
terminology.example: On First Response violation, email LAB_ShiftLead and set SLA_Violated__c.
terminology.non_example: A manual Chatter ping with no milestone clock.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Auto-response (APP-003): create-time customer email, not SLA breach.
terminology.boundary: Workflow versus Flow for actions: reverify current Help.

when_to_use: When agents need reusable Knowledge articles instead of repeating Case comments.
When a customer's Entitlement must attach an entitlement process with Milestones (first response/resolution, max 10).
When agents need Lightning Service Console workspace tabs rather than a standard app.
When Omni-Channel routing should dispatch from a queue based on presence and capacity instead of cherry-picking.
when_not_to_use: Do not use Omni-Channel when a simple APP-003 Queue plus assignment rule already matches a tiny pull-based team.
Do not use a Milestone as a substitute for Email-to-Case or Web-to-Case capture.
Do not treat Service Console as the routing engine, or Knowledge as a Files library (APP-006).
Do not stack more than 10 milestones on one entitlement process, or confuse milestones with classic escalation rules.

interview_questions.question: How do Entitlements and Milestones relate to a Case?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: An Entitlement is the customer's service contract. It applies an entitlement process. Milestones on that process are the clocks—first response, resolution—max 10. The Case shows running milestone states.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not treat Priority as an SLA. I auto-apply when Help's feature fits. I configure milestone actions on complete or violate. Recurrence is a milestone-type choice. Classic escalation can still exist, but I will not name it a milestone. I review Milestone Limitations before promising behavior.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Gold entitlement on LAB_Northwind; Case shows First Response 1 hour.

interview_questions.question: Knowledge versus Files versus Case comments?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Knowledge is published articles with versions and categories. Files are Content documents (APP-006). Case comments are ticket chatter. Only Knowledge is the service corpus.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I attach articles from Console. I do not dump SOPs into a library and call it Knowledge. Public channels need category security. Draft versus published is metadata lifecycle, not a Case field.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Reset_VPN published internally; not a ContentDistribution link.

interview_questions.question: Agents miss first response while sitting in a console app. Design the fix.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Console is not the clock or the router. Put a First Response milestone on the entitlement process and route with Omni-Channel so Available agents actually get the Case.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check whether an entitlement applied. If clocks exist but work sits on a queue, Omni-Channel or disciplined pull is the gap. If no clocks, entitlements are the gap. I keep assignment filling the queue. I do not add a twelfth milestone. I train presence statuses so 'Available' means available.
interview_questions.example: Gold process two milestones; Omni-Channel on LAB_Tier1; Console already in use.

interview_questions.question: A three-person team wants Omni-Channel, Knowledge, and eight milestones next week.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I stage it. Capture and queues first (APP-003). Then two real milestones, then articles, then Omni-Channel if cherry-picking hurts. Eight clocks on day one will not be operated.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help allows up to 10, not 'as many as a slide deck.' I ask which two times customers actually bought. I will not enable public Knowledge casually. Omni-Channel needs presence hygiene. A tiny team can stay on pull queues plus escalation until volume justifies dispatch.
interview_questions.example: Week 1: two milestones auto-apply. Week 2: five VPN articles. Week 3: Omni-Channel pilot.

interview_questions.question: Milestone never starts on new Cases.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check entitlement on the Case, process assignment, auto-apply criteria, and milestone entry criteria such as Status equals New.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I compare a Case with and without entitlement. I look at business hours. I do not rebuild Omni-Channel first. I verify we did not hit a limitation in Milestone Limitations. I check whether IT Services SLA setup was used instead of classic processes in this org.
interview_questions.example: Auto-apply requires Account Type = Customer; LAB_ prospect Cases skipped.
follow_ups: Does Origin Email skip the process?
weak_answer_warnings: Deleting the process as first step

interview_questions.question: Omni-Channel utility shows Available but no work arrives.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check routing configuration, service channel, queue membership, capacity, and whether assignment even put Cases in that queue.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Empty queue means APP-003 assignment/default owner, not Omni. Wrong presence or zero capacity means the dispatcher will not offer work. Console being open is irrelevant if the utility is disconnected. I test with a LAB_ Case I can see in the queue list.
interview_questions.example: Presence Available-Chat while Cases need Available-Cases; capacity 0.

interview_questions.question: When do you keep classic escalation and skip milestones?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When there is no entitlement product, no per-customer SLA, and you only need a manager email if New is stale. That is APP-003. Do not fake entitlements.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The day customers buy Gold vs Silver clocks, I move to entitlement processes. Mixing both without a diagram causes double pages. I still might keep escalation as a backstop for Cases with no entitlement. I cite the 10-milestone cap so they do not design a clock per Status value.
interview_questions.example: Internal IT ticketing with one queue and a 4-hour escalation; no entitlements sold.

interview_questions.question: Teach this with the hotel desk analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: SOP binder is Knowledge, loyalty tier is Entitlement, clocks are Milestones (max 10), desk is Console, dispatcher is Omni-Channel, lobby list is the APP-003 queue.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: It breaks when not every guest has a tier, when Omni routes chats not just Cases, when Knowledge is not a Files vault, and when classic escalation still pages the night manager. I then quote Help on milestone purpose, the cap of 10, recurrence, milestone actions, and auto-apply. I keep assignment as the thing that still fills the lobby.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard: Gold folio with two clocks, article clipped on, dispatcher pushing to a free concierge.
weak_answer_warnings: Generic catalog metaphors instead of the hotel-desk mapping
